assessment: Caffeine is part of a journal title in an author's disclosure. STEPWISE tests an app-supported walking program, with fatigue among its measures. NCT04848077 has no posted results. PMID 37700241 is the protocol, and PMC12625118 analyzes baseline assessments.
SAGE is a publisher of two qualitative research handbooks. The protocol concerns web-based social contact in long-term care.

GaitAge scheduled a coffee break after indoor sensor and walking tests. Methods give no coffee serving or intake measurement. The gait protocol excludes Parkinson's disease. The cohort's later university reports concern outdoor gait sensor validation.
Mobile SAGE-AF is an atrial-fibrillation study cited in the wearable assessment literature. ADAPT measures physical function using sensors in Parkinson's and COPD cohorts.
SAGE is the publisher of a qualitative methods book. The project concerns remote data collection procedures.
SAGE is the publisher of several mixed-methods and interview texts. The DROP trial compares deprescribing support for overactive bladder medications.
Salmon is the surname of an author of NICE digital-health evaluation standards. SmartHeart tests feasibility and acceptability of a home monitoring system for heart failure.
Blackberry is the surname of an author in the cited Parkinson online dance therapy feasibility study, PMID 34587834. UPGRADE-PD compares exercise delivery modes.

Kale is an author in a cited voice-data survey. Caffeine was among suggested pre-recording covariates that the repeated speech example did not collect. It provides no coffee or kale clinical exposure.
Participants beat eggs for one minute as a repetitive wrist movement for smartwatch bradykinesia assessment. Egg consumption is outside the protocol. NCT06817772 has no posted results.

Caffeine use is a baseline personal habit. ChiCTR2400083685 compares stepped herbal medicine and psychotherapy and excludes major neurologic disorders including Parkinson's. The World Sleep 2025 abstract reports insomnia outcomes for the package without a coffee or caffeine comparison.

The ALS protocol restricts caffeine before testing and compares istradefylline with or without intermittent hypoxia. Its cited 10-person trial tests caffeine plus intermittent hypoxia for walking after spinal cord injury, PMID 35686460. Neither supplies brewed coffee or Parkinson fatigue data. NCT05377424 has no posted results.

MiniMeal tests a soup and drink containing bioprocessed oat bran and chickpea in older adults without diagnosed neurodegenerative disease. Physical assessments include standing balance and chair stands. Fall frequency is outside the planned outcome battery. NCT06353984 has no posted results.

Blueberry appears in a cited cognitive supplementation study used to inform sample size. PMID 28221821 tests freeze-dried blueberry powder in adults with mild cognitive impairment and measures memory and fMRI. The MiniMeal protocol includes a gastrointestinal scale with constipation items but assigns no blueberry.
Cherry is an author of a cited occupational therapy trial. The protocol compares combination exercise in healthy older adults and includes cognition measures.
Sage is the publisher of a grounded-theory methods book. The Parkinson trial compares occupational therapy and usual care.
Sage is the publisher of a cited nonverbal communication handbook. The Parkinson cohort investigates social self-management over time.
Sage is the publisher of qualitative methods works. The Parkinson protocol tests partnered ballroom dancing.

The hormone-assay subset was instructed to avoid bananas, caffeine, turkey, and tomatoes the day before testing. KCT0002869 assigns Yokukansankachimpihange or placebo. The cited apathy and anxiety changes concern a related herbal formula. Searches by exact registry ID and title found no outcome report for this trial.
Sage is the publisher of methods references and the journal SAGE Open. The protocol studies self-management after spinal cord injury.

Caffeine is discussed among sleep-hygiene topics in cognitive behavioral therapy and an education control. The population has type 2 diabetes and insomnia. Coffee intake is outside the treatment contrast.

Avoiding caffeine before sleep is example advice in the specialized nursing package. NICE-PD compared added Parkinson nurse specialist care with usual care. NCT03830190 is complete, and the 2025 MDS congress abstract reports overall quality of life and motor estimates without a coffee comparison.
SAGE is the publisher of a cited qualitative methods text. The mixed-methods protocol evaluates virtual services for neurological populations.
Sage is a publisher in the qualitative methods bibliography. The Swedish cohort studies housing, relocation, and aging.

Millet is a surname in a cerebrospinal fluid assay citation. Salmon is a surname in a cited verbal learning study. The longitudinal protocol studies neurocognitive and pulmonary outcomes after COVID-19.
SAGE is the publisher of a cited health psychology chapter. The trial tests an exercise intervention in healthy adults.

Chicken appears in the phrase chicken and egg used to describe direction of causation in a statistical model. SAGE publishes cited qualitative methods books. The study concerns posttraumatic epilepsy and family caregiving.
SAGE is a publisher in the qualitative methods references. The single-group trial tests an internet-delivered insomnia intervention for caregivers.
Sage is the publisher of a qualitative research book. The Dortmund Vital Study evaluates cognition and work ability across adulthood.

The caffeine reference leads to an isolated-caffeine trial, PMID 22855866, with fatigue measured separately from sleepiness.
SAGE is a publisher of mixed-methods research guidance. The protocol identifies suitable remote concussion assessment measures.
